cards.de: The government has announced a reform.
cards.fr: ___ gouvernement a annoncé une réforme.
cards.note: Nouns ending in -ment are masculine: le gouvernement, le bâtiment, le changement. The ending is a reliable clue, so use it.

cards.de: She is wearing a white blouse.
cards.fr: Elle porte une chemise ___.
cards.note: The feminine of blanc is blanche. chemise is singular, so the adjective stays singular too.

cards.de: I'm phoning her (my sister).
cards.fr: Je ___ téléphone.
cards.note: téléphoner à qn takes an indirect object, so lui or leur. The same goes for répondre à qn and parler à qn.

cards.de: We start at nine o'clock.
cards.fr: Nous ___ à neuf heures.
cards.note: Verbs in -cer take a cedilla before o and a: nous commençons, je commençais. Without it, the c would sound like k.

cards.de: When I was little, I went to the seaside every summer.
cards.fr: Quand j'étais petit, ___ à la mer chaque été.
cards.note: A repeated habit in the past takes the imparfait. chaque été is the giveaway. Before a vowel je becomes j': j'allais.

cards.de: I like going to the cinema at the weekend.
cards.fr: J'aime ___ au cinéma le week-end.
cards.note: After aimer, adorer, détester, vouloir, pouvoir, devoir and espérer the infinitive follows with no preposition.

cards.de: She works in Lyon.
cards.fr: Elle travaille ___ Lyon.
cards.note: City names always take à, never en: à Lyon, à Berlin, à Rome.

cards.de: I buy
cards.note: e becomes è before a silent ending: j'achète, ils achètent. But nous achetons, vous achetez.
The plus-que-parfait is used after si for an unreal past. Verbs of movement like venir form it with être, and the participle agrees.

English says "they got married" with no reflexive pronoun and no agreement, but French reflexive verbs always take être in the passé composé and the participle agrees with the subject: ils se sont mariés, elles se sont mariées.
afin que requires the subjonctif: Je vous envoie le plan afin que vous puissiez nous trouver. pouvoir is irregular: puisse, puisses, puisse, puissions, puissiez, puissent.
The stem is irregular: devr-. je devrais means "I should" and is the polite way to give advice.

cards.de: they call (on the phone)
cards.note: The l doubles before a silent ending: j'appelle, ils appellent. But nous appelons.
The conditionnel présent goes in the main clause after si + imparfait. pouvoir has the irregular stem pourr- plus imparfait endings.

cards.de: Nature is magnificent in autumn.
cards.fr: Le nature est magnifique en automne.
cards.answer: La nature est magnifique en automne.
cards.note: Nouns ending in -ure are feminine: la nature, la voiture, la culture. Le mur is not an exception, as it has no -ure.

cards.de: a new car
cards.fr: une nouvel voiture
cards.note: nouvel exists only in the masculine before a vowel. With a feminine noun you always use nouvelle.

cards.fr: Je lui aide.
cards.note: aider qn takes a direct object, so the pronoun is le, la or les, never lui.

cards.de: I get up at six o'clock.
cards.fr: Je me léve à six heures.
cards.answer: Je me lève à six heures.
cards.note: The accent here leans the other way: e becomes è, not é. Same pattern in je me promène and il achète.

cards.de: The sun was shining and the birds were singing.
cards.fr: Le soleil a brillé et les oiseaux ont chanté.
cards.answer: Le soleil brillait et les oiseaux chantaient.
cards.note: Descriptions of scenery, weather and mood take the imparfait. The passé composé would report them as single finished events.

cards.de: I am waiting for the bus at the stop.
cards.fr: J'attends sur le bus à l'arrêt.
cards.note: attendre takes a direct object with no preposition. The for of English wait for easily tempts you into adding one.

cards.de: I'm waiting for him outside the cinema.
cards.fr: Je ___ attends devant le cinéma.
cards.note: attendre qn takes no preposition, so the pronoun is direct: le, la, les. Before a vowel, le becomes l'.

cards.de: Man braucht zwei Stunden, um dorthin zu kommen.
cards.fr: Il ___ deux heures pour y aller.
cards.note: falloir only exists impersonally: il faut. It covers English "you need", "you have to" and "it takes".

cards.de: When it rains, I always take the bus.
cards.fr: Quand il ___, je prends toujours le bus.
cards.note: For habits, quand means "whenever" and takes the présent. The futur only appears when you really are talking about the future.

cards.de: Recently my brother has begun to take an interest in politics.
cards.fr: Depuis peu, mon frère commence à ___.
cards.note: The verb takes à: s'intéresser à qc. The noun l'intérêt takes pour instead: l'intérêt pour la politique.

cards.de: I didn't find a single mistake.
cards.fr: Je n'ai trouvé ___ faute.
cards.note: aucun/aucune is always singular and takes no article. It replaces pas de and stresses not a single one.

cards.de: My grandmother is ninety-seven years old.
cards.fr: Ma grand-mère a ___ ans.
cards.note: Built as 4 times 20 plus 17. In Belgium and Switzerland people say nonante-sept.

cards.fr: J'ai acheté un kilo de cerises au marché.
cards.answer: J'ai acheté une livre de cerises au marché.
cards.note: La livre is the pound (weight or currency) and is feminine. Le livre is the book.

cards.fr: Un vieux monsieur attend devant la porte.
cards.task: Put into the feminine: une dame.
cards.answer: Une vieille dame attend devant la porte.
cards.note: vieux becomes vieille in the feminine. Other adjectives with their own feminine forms: roux → rousse, doux → douce.

cards.fr: J'ai vu Marie hier.
cards.note: The pronoun goes before the auxiliary. The participle agrees with a direct object that comes before it: vue.

cards.fr: Tu appelles ta sœur tous les soirs.
cards.answer: Vous appelez votre sœur tous les soirs.
cards.note: With nous and vous the ending is pronounced, so a single l is enough: nous appelons, vous appelez.

cards.fr: Il fait nuit et je marche seul quand une voiture s'arrête devant moi.
cards.task: Put into the past: background in the imparfait, the event in the passé composé.
cards.answer: Il faisait nuit et je marchais seul quand une voiture s'est arrêtée devant moi.
cards.note: The setting (night, walking) continues in the imparfait, while the event that breaks in goes into the passé composé.

cards.fr: Elle pense à ses prochaines vacances.
cards.task: Replace « à ses prochaines vacances » with a pronoun.
cards.note: With things, a phrase introduced by à is replaced by y, and one introduced by de by en: Elle en parle.

cards.de: This decision was a mistake.
accept: Cette décision a été une erreur.
cards.note: Like -tion, the ending -sion is feminine: la décision, la télévision, la discussion. Hence cette décision, not ce décision.

cards.de: That is a beautiful story.
cards.note: The feminine is always belle, even before a vowel. Only the masculine has the special form bel.

cards.de: Can you explain it to them?
accept: Est-ce que tu peux le leur expliquer ?
cards.note: With two verbs the pronouns go directly before the infinitive, not before the conjugated verb.

cards.de: I pay by card.
cards.note: Verbs in -ayer allow both spellings: je paie or je paye. The form with i is more common today.

cards.de: I wanted to call you, but I didn't have your number.
cards.answer: Je voulais t'appeler, mais je n'avais pas ton numéro.
accept: Je voulais t'appeler mais je n'avais pas ton numéro.
Je voulais te téléphoner, mais je n'avais pas ton numéro.
cards.note: vouloir and avoir describe an intention and a state here, so the imparfait fits. J'ai voulu t'appeler would mean you actually made the attempt.

cards.de: Do not forget to call me tomorrow.
accept: N'oublie pas de me téléphoner demain.
cards.note: oublier de faire qc. Before a noun there is no de: J'ai oublié mon parapluie.

Every noun in -isme is masculine, with no exceptions. The final -e still pulls you towards la, which is why the feminine -ise words sit next to them here: la crise, la valise, la surprise. The ending decides, not the last letter.

Naturel and personnel double the l, moyen doubles the n, and étranger takes the grave accent -ère. The two to memorise are public → publique (qu keeps the k sound) and bref → brève, which changes f to v and adds an accent.

cards.task: Both pronouns, in the right order
cards.note: Watch the switch: me, te and nous come before le, la, les (me le, te les, nous en), but lui and leur come after them (le lui, la leur), and en always sits last. The imperative Rends-le-moi flips everything: the object goes after the verb and me becomes moi.
Only the second é flips to è, and only when the ending is silent, so préfère and préfèrent contrast with préférons and préférez. The first é never moves.

Chaque été triggers the imparfait for repetition (allions), while lundi dernier and tout de suite point to one finished event. Note that pleuvait is the background to je lisais, and est arrivé takes être while ont commencé takes avoir.
Profiter de, dépendre de and avoir besoin de all take de, while participer à and s'intéresser à take à. Regarder needs nothing, so no à or de creeps in after it.

cards.de: courage
cards.note: Masculine. Nouns ending in -age are almost always masculine: le voyage, le fromage. Exceptions: la page, la plage, l'image (f).

cards.de: the shop, the store
cards.note: False friend: a magazine you read is le magazine. Faire les magasins means to go shopping.

cards.de: the problem
cards.note: Masculine despite the final -e. Nouns of Greek origin ending in -ème are masculine: le système, le thème.

cards.de: the lycée (French upper secondary school)
cards.note: Masculine despite the -ée ending, like le musée: aller au lycée. Students there are des lycéens et des lycéennes.

cards.de: water
cards.note: An important exception: nouns ending in -eau are normally masculine, but l'eau is feminine. So une eau minérale and l'eau est froide.

cards.de: the sentence (words)
cards.note: False friend: une phrase is a full sentence. An English phrase is une expression or une locution.
